title: How radio carries sound: AM and FM
examples: What is the difference between AM and FM?
Why can I hear far-away AM stations at night?

figure.name: x-wave
figure.note: A carrier wave shaped by the sound

explain.say: A radio station sends a steady carrier wave and changes its shape to carry the sound. There are two main ways to do that: AM and FM.

draw.text: How radio carries sound: AM and FM

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A carrier wave shaped by the sound

explain.say: In AM, amplitude modulation, the height of the wave rises and falls with the sound. It is simple, but crackle from storms and machines also changes the height.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A carrier wave shaped by the sound

explain.say: In FM, frequency modulation, the height stays fixed and the waves are squeezed closer or spread apart. The radio reads only the spacing, so most crackle is ignored.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A carrier wave shaped by the sound

explain.say: So FM sounds clearer and is used for music, while AM's longer waves travel much further, especially at night.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: FM sounds clearer; AM reaches further.

faq.a: AM means amplitude modulation. The height of the carrier wave is made to rise and fall in step with the sound, so louder moments make taller waves.
FM means frequency modulation. The wave's height stays the same, but the waves are squeezed closer together or spread apart in step with the sound.

faq.q: Why does FM sound clearer than AM?
faq.a: Electrical noise from lightning and machines mostly changes a wave's height. FM ignores the height and reads only the spacing of the waves, so most crackle is thrown away.

faq.q: Why can AM stations be heard so far away?
faq.a: AM uses longer waves, which bend around the Earth's curve and, at night, bounce off a high layer of the atmosphere called the ionosphere. So they can travel hundreds or thousands of kilometres.
asks: Why do I hear distant stations at night?

faq.a: It is a steady radio wave at the station's own frequency. On its own it carries nothing; the sound is added by shaping it, its height in AM or its spacing in FM.
asks: What does the station number on the dial mean?

facts: FM radio stations broadcast at around 88 to 108 megahertz.
AM medium-wave stations broadcast at roughly 0.5 to 1.7 megahertz, with waves hundreds of metres long.

options.say: The spacing of the waves, its frequency

quiz.why: Frequency modulation keeps the height fixed and changes how closely the waves are packed, in step with the sound.
